name: Zechariah

objectives.text: Identify Zechariah as a prophet God sent to encourage his people while they rebuilt the temple
Retell Zechariah's promise that Jerusalem's King would come riding on a donkey and match it to Jesus entering Jerusalem
Recite Zechariah 4:6 and explain that God's work is accomplished by his Spirit rather than by human strength
Describe God's call through Zechariah for his people to return to him and his promise to return to them
Describe how the LORD removed Joshua the high priest's filthy garments and clothed him in clean ones as a picture of God taking away sin
Explain the vision of the lampstand and two olive trees and its message to Zerubbabel about not despising the day of small things
Summarize Zechariah's answer to the question about fasting by listing the justice, mercy, and truthfulness God required of his people
Locate Zechariah in the history of the return from exile and explain how he and Haggai together urged the rebuilding of the temple
Compare the worthless shepherds of Zechariah 11 with the Good Shepherd Jesus describes in John 10
Summarize each of the eight night visions and state the message of comfort or warning each gave the returned exiles
Explain Zechariah's promise that many nations would join themselves to the LORD and connect it to the spread of the gospel to the Gentiles
Analyze how the cleansing of Joshua in Zechariah 3 illustrates the Reformed doctrine of justification by imputed righteousness
Interpret the symbols of the night visions using the explanations the angel gives within the text as a method for reading apocalyptic literature
Explain how the Branch of Zechariah 3 and 6 unites the offices of priest and king and how the church has read this as fulfilled in Christ
Trace the New Testament quotations of Zechariah in the Gospel passion narratives and explain what each shows about Jesus
Analyze how the prophecy of mourning for the pierced one and the fountain opened for cleansing portrays repentance and forgiveness
Evaluate proposed explanations for Matthew's attribution of the thirty pieces of silver prophecy to Jeremiah
Evaluate how the Book of Revelation takes up and transforms Zechariah's imagery of horses, lampstands, olive trees, and measuring
Evaluate arguments about the unity and authorship of Zechariah 1-8 and 9-14 and defend the traditional view of the book as one prophetic work
Compare major interpretive approaches to the Day of the LORD in Zechariah 14 and explain the significance of Holiness to the LORD extending to all of life
Compose an essay synthesizing how Zechariah's portraits of the lowly King, the stricken Shepherd, and the pierced One anticipate the suffering and reign of the Messiah

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (donkey King, Zechariah 4:6, lampstand vision, shepherds, night visions, Branch, thirty pieces of silver, temple rebuilding, Revelation imagery, unity of the book, the pierced one). Dropped vague or affective filler (strange dreams, God cares about Jerusalem, applying the Spirit helping us). Replaced the list-building objective with tracing New Testament quotations. Added missing content: the call to return (1:3-6), Joshua's cleansing and justification (ch 3), the fasting question and required justice (chs 7-8), nations joining the LORD (2:11, 8:20-23), interpreting apocalyptic symbols, the fountain for cleansing (13:1), Matthew's Jeremiah attribution, and Zechariah 14. Anchored objectives to specific verses and to Westminster and Heidelberg articles where they state the doctrine taught.
